newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin, Chirac meeting to go ahead as planned.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Chirac meeting to go ahead as planned.

text.p: A meeting between Russian Prime Minister Boris Yeltsin and French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday morning will go ahead as planned, a French spokeswoman said.
News that the Russia-France bilateral meeting was to go ahead should allay concerns about the Russian leader's condition after Yeltsin cut short his program Saturday night.

Yeltsin unexpectedly missed a gala concert during the Group of Seven leaders summit Saturday and officials said he was tired. Yeltsin left a dinner about 20 minutes ahead of G7 leaders. Journalists had been told the leaders would all leave together.
A Russian delegation source said the president, who spent eight months out of office from the middle of last year after heart problems, surgery and pneumonia, was tired.
A Kremlin official said: "He is in his residence, he decided that he would prefer not to take part in this event." But he added: "Tomorrow's (Sunday's) meetings will go ahead according to plan."
